svg.text: A convincing way to find undervalued papers, and why it fails
GitHub stars against upvotes for every feed paper carrying both. The labelled points are the largest residuals in each
Fits well — r = 0.47 on 9,868 papers — and both tails are measurement artifacts, not undervalued or overvalued ideas.
High side: an established project posts a technical report and the report inherits the repo's whole star history. Low side: the linked repo is a stub.
Not double-attribution — 10,076 papers hold 10,076 distinct repos, one each. The problem is the repo's age, not its reuse.
Repo dates fetched 2026-09-14 for the labelled points. Legitimate ones are made FOR the paper; the rest are years older, and Mixtral's is newer than its paper.
At scale this needs created_at for all 10,076 repos — 60 requests/hour unauthenticated, so it needs a token.
